title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: EDDIE'S TRUCK
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Eddie Ruiz, a tow truck driver from Fresno, California.
Eddie can fix any breakdown in the valley, except one. Him and his big brother, Manny.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BREAKDOWN
segments.quote: In taking revenge, a man is but even with his enemy; but in passing it over, he is superior.
segments.author: Francis Bacon
lines: When their dad passed, both brothers wanted his old blue pickup. Eddie got it. Two years of silence.
Then Big Blue died on Highway Ninety-Nine. In the glove box, Dad's old Francis Bacon book had one line circled:
In taking revenge, a man is but even with his enemy; but in passing it over, he is superior.
Silence was revenge. Eddie drove to Manny's shop.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE SHOP DOOR
segments.quote: If you are wrong, admit it quickly and emphatically.
segments.author: Dale Carnegie
lines: Manny stood in the doorway. Shop's closed, he said. To you.
Eddie had a speech ready about who was right. Then he remembered Dale Carnegie:
If you are wrong, admit it quickly and emphatically.
So he did. I didn't want the truck, he said. I wanted Dad.
Manny was quiet a long time. Then: Bring it Saturday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE ENGINE
segments.quote: The real cycle you're working on is a cycle called yourself.
segments.author: Robert M. Pirsig
lines: Saturday, Eddie rushed and dropped a bolt into the engine. Twice.
Manny tapped a dusty book by Robert Pirsig, a writer who loved motorcycles:
The real cycle you're working on is a cycle called yourself.
So Eddie slowed down, held the flashlight, and came back every Saturday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: ROUND TWO
segments.quote: The aim of an argument or discussion should not be victory, but progress.
segments.author: Joseph Joubert
lines: Then they fought again. Was Dad's favorite station country or oldies?
Eddie's wife Carmen, holding tacos, read them Joseph Joubert, a French writer:
The aim of an argument or discussion should not be victory, but progress.
So they turned on Dad's old radio to settle it. The ball game. Of course.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE DENT
segments.quote: Laughter is not at all a bad beginning for a friendship, and it is far the best ending for one.
segments.author: Oscar Wilde
lines: Under the tailgate, Eddie found a dent and turned red. At sixteen, I hit a mailbox, he said, and blamed you.
Manny laughed so hard he sat on a tire. Dad knew. He made me wash it anyway.
Carmen quoted Oscar Wilde:
Laughter is not at all a bad beginning for a friendship, and it is far the best ending for one.
They left the dent right where it was.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE ROAD
segments.quote: We find after years of struggle that we do not take a trip; a trip takes us.
segments.author: John Steinbeck
lines: In October, Big Blue roared to life. Whose truck was it now?
Eddie thought of John Steinbeck, who drove across America in a pickup:
We find after years of struggle that we do not take a trip; a trip takes us.
So two brothers drove one truck to the coast, ball game on.
Now Big Blue spends a month in Fresno, a month in Visalia.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Let it go. Say sorry. Slow down. Argue for progress. Laugh. Take the trip.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Let it go. Say sorry. Slow down. Argue for progress. Laugh together. Take the trip.
My brother and I share a car too. Mostly, we share the parking tickets.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
